title: Migrate input semantics to adaptive density and touch-target parity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Audit and migration of input surface semantics to support an adaptive density system that preserves touch-target parity across desktop and mobile. This ticket scopes token changes, component API compatibility, validation timing semantics, and accessibility adjustments so that compact and regular densities behave consistently with keyboard, pointer, and assistive tech. Goal: a migration plan + implementation guidance for engineering and design to roll out in console-2025.03 with minimal visual regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Token mapping defined: legacy sizing tokens -> adaptive density tokens
All input variants (text, textarea, select, toggle) respect minimum 44px touch target on mobile while visual density may be compact on desktop
Validation and helper text behavior documented (timing, priority, animation suppression) and implemented as feature-flagged rollout
Keyboard focus, screen reader labels, and ARIA invalid states are preserved for backward compatibility
Design QA checklist and automated visual snapshot suite added to catch regressions
design_notes: We discovered multiple inconsistencies: compact mode previously reduced hit targets below recommended touch sizes; helper rows collapsed unexpectedly when placeholder + suffix present; validation animations clashed with motion-reduced preference. Proposal: introduce two new semantic tokens -- --rdw-input-min-target and --rdw-input-visual-scale -- controlled by density token sets. Implement CSS layering where min-target enforces pointer area without changing visual padding (use ::after hit area). Keep existing component props (density: 'regular'|'compact') but map them to the new tokens and provide a compatibility shim for older consumers.
decisions: Introduce --rdw-input-min-target (px) enforced at hit-test layer, separate from visual padding
Use --rdw-input-visual-scale for font-size and icon sizing adjustments in compact mode
Delay microcopy changes to a follow-up ticket; this task focuses on interaction and tokens
Feature flag rollout (flags: forms.adaptive_density, forms.compact_compat) to allow gradual adoption
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): internal apps only behind forms.adaptive_density for 2 weeks. Phase 2: open to beta customers and enable visual snapshot checks. Phase 3: default on for new accounts, opt-in toggle for existing orgs for one month, then migrate with notification. Engineering to coordinate migrations with Dedicated and Private teams to ensure CSS/asset parity.
